title: Posts start the spindle (S0 M3) on a probe tool

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
The Tormach post starts the spindle for every tool, including a probe. A probing operation posts:

```
T7 M6
G43 H7
S0 M3
```

Found while preparing the #500 Hub check (`test-500-tormach-probe-guard.nc`). The block comes from `startPreamble()` in `assets/posts/tormach.cps` (`block(["S" + ni(sRpm), "M3"])`), which is the same on main. It is not something #500 added.

**Why it matters:** a wireless touch probe must never be spun. At S0 the spindle should not turn, but the program still commands it on. That relies on the control treating S0 as stopped, and any spindle-override or minimum-RPM behaviour turns it into a spinning probe. A probe tool should get no `S`/`M3` at all, and an `M5` if the previous tool left the spindle running.

**Check the other posts too:** fanuc, haas, mazak, sinumerik and heidenhain may share the same pattern.

Done means: a probe-tool section posts no spindle start (and stops a running spindle) in every post that handles probing, pinned by a post test on a probing program per affected post.

title: Depth ladders start with a feed pass at Top - an air pass when Top is the material top

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while fixing #510 (PR #513). The shared level helper `cut_levels(top, bottom, step)` starts every depth-stepping ladder at Top: pocket, contour, circular, trace, face, slot and the 3D entries. When Top is the material's top surface, which is the default for most 2D ops, the first level is a full feed pass in air. For example, a Slot with top 20, bottom 10 and step 5 cuts at [20, 15, 10]. That's never a gouge, but it's a wasted pass at feed rate on every op.

**Question for the owner:** should the first level be `top - step` (giving [15, 10]), or should an air pass be skipped only when Top is at the material top?

Either change moves most CL and NC goldens, so it should be one deliberate change across every ladder, not per op.

Done means: a decision recorded; if yes, every ladder starts one step below Top (or skips the air level), goldens are regenerated in one commit, and the change is pinned by a ladder test.

title: Slot: a typed Slot whose cutter rides its round cap is convicted of a gouge on every move

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while working #35 (pocket/slot recognition).

**What happens:** a typed 2D Slot whose cutter reaches its round cap is reported as a gouge on every cutting move, with no part model in the document at all, so its path never posts.

**Reproduced on `main` 7e907afa** (headless, app layer): new world, `SetStock` box 80 x 60 x 20, `AddTool` `EM-0600-4FL`, `CreateOperation` Slot on `SrcRef::Stock` with `a = (-15, 0)`, `b = (15, 0)`, `top_z` fixed 20, `bottom_z` fixed 10, stepdown 5, then `GenerateOperation`:
- width 6 (cutter = width, one pass along the centreline): `Gouge` at moves 2, 3, 7, 8, 12, 13 (the plunge and the feed of every level);
- width 10 (rings at +-2): `Gouge` on every feed of every level.

**Likely cause (not confirmed):** the Slot's machining region is `operation::stadium(a, b, width / 2)` with `CAP_SEGMENTS = 16` chords per semicircle, inscribed in the true arc. The tangency law (b) in `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs` wants d(centre, boundary) >= r - tol with `GOUGE_TOL = 0.01`, but a centre on the cap's centre sits only r * cos(5.625 deg) from a chord: 3 mm cutter radius -> 2.9855 < 2.99, a 0.0145 mm "bite" that is pure chord error. The generator's passes ride the true arc, so the verdict convicts a tangent cutter.

**Done means:** a Slot whose passes are tangent to its own stadium verifies clean (no `Gouge`), while a Slot driven past its walls still does; pinned by a test that generates the width-6 and width-10 cases above and asserts no `Gouge`, plus one oversize case that is still convicted.

Related: #35's recognised slots create Slot operations and inherit this until it is fixed (their tests pin the path geometry exactly instead of the verifier's verdict).

title: Fixture box laws judge an XY arc by its inscribed chords at the bare band radius, missing steel within the arc's sagitta

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while gating #339 slice 2 (whether the mesh law needs to convict).

**What happens:** the box fixture laws (`stack_span::band_struck`, via `Move::segments3` at `GOUGE_TOL` 0.01) sweep an XY arc's **inscribed** chords using each band's bare radius. The true arc bulges outward past every chord by up to the chord's sagitta, so fixture steel inside that sliver is not seen.

**Measured:** an R30 arc with an r3 flute has a sagitta of 0.008–0.010 mm. With a box face half a sagitta inside the tool's true reach (the tool really goes 0.004–0.005 mm into it), `bands_vs_fixtures` returns no hit. This affects every fixture box. #339's mesh law can't help, because it only reads moves the box flagged (though its own arc reading already pads by sagitta plus `ARC_PAD`).

**Fix:** pad `band_struck`'s radius per arc piece by that piece's sagitta, as `mesh_steel::chords` already does. Check XZ/YZ arcs and the posed chord walk the same way. #413 (XY arcs drawn as inside chords in the field engine and envelope scan) is the same family.

**Done means:** an arc reaching a fixture by less than its sagitta reports `FixtureHit`; straight-move verdicts are unchanged; existing fixture suites keep their verdicts.

title: Box fixture laws may miss hits on a spindle-C turning move: stamp_c pieces keep the whole move's tool axis

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Safety or crash: wrong output, gouge, data loss

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while writing #339 slice 3 (fixture mesh for posed and C moves). Not yet reproduced as a missed hit, hence P1 pending a repro. It becomes P0 if a repro shows a real hit passing the post gate.

**What the code does:** `cl::stamp_c` splits a turning (spindle-C) move into pieces that all keep the whole move's stated tool axis. On every piece but the last, that axis is off the live-tool station by the rest of the turn. The box fixture laws read the stated axis. For C moves they also judge on the part-frame chord, even for **fixed** steel, which stays in the machine frame. Either can put the judged tool stack somewhere other than where the machine puts it, so a real hit on fixed steel (a tailstock, a fixed clamp) could be missed.

**Why #339's mesh law can't cover it:** it only ever clears box hits, so it cannot add the missing ones. Slice 3 reads C moves at the machine station for fixed steel, but only to clear hits. See `docs/decisions/339-mesh-posed.md` on the #339 branches.

**Done means:**
- A test with a C turning move past fixed steel near the station, judged by the box laws, reports the hit the machine would make; or a demonstration that it can't happen, with the reasoning pinned.
- `stamp_c` pieces carry their own interpolated axis, or the laws read C moves in the machine frame for fixed steel.

title: Reconsider committing UI pixel snapshots as test data

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

body:
Raised by the maintainer (2026-11-09): "We should reconsider the committing of snapshots as test data".

## Why
The shell pixel snapshots (`crates/ui/tests/snapshots/egui_app.png`, `egui_app_light.png`, `egui_tool_editor.png`) cost more than they catch:
- **Every UI PR conflicts on them.** Today #296, #349, #466 and #467 all needed a merge plus a regenerate just for these binaries. Git can't merge a PNG.
- **A version bump turned main red** (#448/#449). The toolbar label is now pinned for tests, but any other incidental pixel change does the same.
- **Platform anti-aliasing differs** (#255). Goldens made on Windows fail on macOS for an unchanged tree, so contributors on other OSes can't keep them green.
- **They catch little.** A failure is "23 pixels differ"; the test doesn't say what broke.

## Options (to research and decide)
1. **Structural UI tests in the PR flow, pixel snapshots only at the cut.** This is what #359 proposes: the ignored pixel tests run in the release tier on the reference OS, and the structural tests (widget present, order, labels, via the egui test harness) run per PR. The PNGs stay committed but are refreshed once per cut, not per PR.
2. **Stop committing the PNGs.** Generate a baseline on a reference machine (or as a CI artifact on a manual workflow) and compare locally. No binaries in git, but the baseline has to be fetched.
3. **Keep the PNGs, never merge them.** `.gitattributes`: `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/*.png binary merge=ours`, plus a rule that a branch regenerates its snapshots after `git merge origin/main`. Conflicts disappear, and the regenerate step stays manual.
4. **Git LFS for snapshots.** Smaller clones, but conflicts are no better, and it adds an LFS dependency for contributors.

Recommendation to evaluate: **1 + 3**. Merge #359 (structural tests per PR, pixel lane at the cut) and add the `merge=ours` attribute meanwhile, so snapshot PNGs never block a merge.

## Done means
The open questions are answered here, a decision is recorded, and sub-issues are filed (e.g. "merge #359", "add .gitattributes for snapshots", "update AGENTS.md Testing / gate tiers"). Then this umbrella closes, per the needs-research law.

Related: #359, #255, #448, #449.

title: Built-in VMC 3-axis blocks posting: Z stroke compared in the wrong coordinate frame
body:
The built-in **VMC 3-axis** machine (`assets/machines/vmc.mch`, mounted from the machine picker) states Z travel as `-500..0`. The posting limit check reads that stroke in **program coordinates through the active work offset** — so every move above the Z0 work origin is out of stroke: every retract, clearance and rapid gets reported, and posting is refused.

**Repro** (headless `camcraft-cli mcp`, current main `586092a8`): a 2D Contour on a 1 mm plate with normal clearance moves, document machine = built-in VMC 3-axis, `open_project` → `generate` → `verify`:

```
machine VMC 3-AXIS: 40 limit problem(s): 2D Contour1: move 0 reaches 26.000 in Z, the stroke is -500.000..0.000; ...
```

All 40 problems block the post. The program is clean: rapid at Z+26, approach at Z+3, cuts at Z 0..1 — physically well inside a 500 mm Z column on any real VMC.

**Why:** `-500..0` only makes sense in a machine frame zeroed at the top of the Z column. The checker converts moves to work-offset coordinates (`(w - origin[k]) * sign`, `crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs:337`) and compares them against the file's numbers directly; the module doc (lines 21-25) even states travel is read in program coordinates, but the `.mch` grammar offers no anchor tying a machine-frame stroke to a work offset. The #373 inverted-axis work handles sign only (`program_travel`, `crates/post/src/machine/direction.rs:87`) — the frame clash stands.

Notes:

- Each move is reported twice (both endpoints trip).
- X (±300) / Y (±250) follow the same convention: they pass only when the work origin happens to sit at table center.
- The default `3axis-vmc.mch` states no travel at all — an unstated limit checks nothing — so the same program passes on that def. Whether this check is signal or noise depends on which shipped def you mount. (Older saved projects whose embedded def lacks the Z travel line pass through for the same accidental reason; current builds round-trip the numbers faithfully.)

Fix directions, your call:

1. Restate the bundled def's numbers in the checker's documented convention — but a correct program-coords Z max is inherently work-offset-dependent, which the file cannot know.
2. Add a machine-frame anchor key to `.mch` that the checker converts through — #373's sign handling shows the seam already exists to extend.
3. Or drop `travel` from `vmc.mch` (like `3axis-vmc.mch`) so the default mount doesn't ship a check that contradicts its own convention.

title: Field engine and envelope scan still draw XY arcs as inside chords (follow-up to #402)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
PR #402's fix makes the **column engine** (`Dexel`, which feeds the post gate's verdict) sweep XY arcs on the true circle. Two other places still draw XY arcs as chords **inside** the arc, and they carry the same two-sided error.
- **Convex corners:** the simulated tool centre comes up to one sagitta closer to the part than the real G2/G3, which produces false cuts.
- **Concave corners and bull-nose helices:** it stops up to one sagitta short, which hides real cuts. #402's `arc_sweep` tests found a bull-nose helix column the true arc cuts 2.5 mm deep that the field engine misses.

**Where**
- `field_cut::chords`: the field engine, used for display and the lathe/rotary views.
- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan.rs`: the generator-time envelope scan.

Neither feeds the post gate's verdict, so nothing unsafe reaches G-code today. But the displayed stock and the generator-time envelope readings can differ from the posted motion by up to one sagitta in either direction.

**Proposed:** reuse #402's exact arc sweep (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/dexel_arc.rs`) or its closed-form reach window in both places. Then tighten `stock_bull_nose::both_engines_cut_a_bull_nose_alike` back to full engine parity on arcs; #402 relaxed it to `arc_parity`.

**Done means**
- The field engine and the envelope scan cut XY arcs on the true circle.
- The engines agree on arcs to the same 1e-5 as on straight moves.
- A concave and a convex corner case are pinned in each.

Follows #402.

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Follow-up from #343 (per-setup machine and post).

**What it should be:**

title: Post gate refuses every 2D Chamfer and Deburr: the program sim judges the intended edge break as a gouge
body:
A 2D Chamfer or a Deburr generates with no warnings, but the post gate refuses it as a gouge. The program sim judges the edge break the operation exists to cut against the model's sharp edge. So no chamfer or deburr program can post whenever the sim judges it, which is any milled program in a box or model stock.

### Measured (main 8f30bee, scratch app test, the commands only)

Part: the 40 x 20 x 10 brick from `operations.rs`'s deburr test (`cube((-20,-10,0), (20,10,10))`). Stock: `FromModel` of the brick, a finished part, so nothing else is cut. Tool: `CM-0600-90`.

| Operation | Generator verify | Post gate |
|---|---|---|
| 2D Chamfer, kind defaults (width 0.8, 45 deg, side auto, top of model) | **0 warnings** | `gouge: program cuts below the model in 624 cell(s), worst 0.74 mm at (19.94, -9.81, z 9.26)` |
| Deburr, the suite's own params (width 2, window z 6..8) | 3 `RapidInStock` (a separate bug, filed separately) | `gouge: ... 1544 cell(s), worst 3.80 mm` |

For the Deburr I binned the gouge columns by depth: **1455 of the 1544 are 2 mm deep or less**. That's the 2 mm chamfer band itself; the 89 deeper ones are where its link rapid drags the cone. So even with clean links the deburr can't post.

### Why

- `stock_sim::simulate_document` judges the simulated stock against "the part as the machine must leave it": every model's facets, minus stock and fixtures (`stock_sim.rs`). `deviate_field` then charges every column cut more than `DEV_TOL` (0.01 mm) below the model as a gouge.
- The model has a sharp edge, and the chamfer and deburr ops cut a bevel into it by design. `operation/generate.rs` already says so for the leave-stock rule ("the chamfer cone owns its face outright", "the deburr cone owns its break outright"), but nothing tells the program sim.

### Possible fixes (owner's call: this is the gouge law)

1. **The ops own their break.** Before `deviate`, take each Chamfer2D or Deburr op's own swept cone (from its path and tool) away from the judged target, so their cut is "finished part" and anything else that cuts there is still judged. This keeps the gate strict everywhere else.
2. **A per-op allowance**: columns cut only by a chamfer or deburr op, within its stated width, are clean. That's simpler, but it needs per-column provenance in the sim.
3. If the intent is that a chamfer must be modelled in CAD first, the ops should refuse at generate ("the model has no chamfer here") instead of passing verify and failing at post.

A pinning test is the brick plus each op: it posts, and a deliberately deeper chamfer (width past the tool's reach, or a cone pushed into the wall) is still refused.

**Root cause (confirmed):** `simulate_document` judges against the model's facets only, and `deviate_field` charges every column cut more than 0.01 mm below them. Measured: 1455 of the deburr's 1544 gouge columns are 2 mm deep or less (its own break), and the 2D Chamfer gives 624 columns with a 0.74 mm worst and 0 generator warnings.

Suggested labels (I can't set them): `bug`, `P1`, `area:sim`, `area:2d`, `area:3d`, `source:agent`.

title: Post gate refuses a clean 2D Contour: the program sim reads a column 9 um inside a vertical wall as a full-height gouge
body:
A 2D Contour around the repo's own `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` generates with no warnings, but the post is refused for a 10 mm gouge that isn't there. The program sim reads a column whose centre is 9 µm inside a vertical wall as cut to the floor.

### Reproduce (main 8f30bee, `camcraft-cli mcp`, one line each)

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"import_model","arguments":{"name":"part","path":"testdata/models/Milling-test.step"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"set_stock","arguments":{"from_model":"part"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"add_tool","arguments":{"catalog":"EM-0600-4FL"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"add_operation","arguments":{"kind":"contour","tool":"EM-0600-4FL","source":"part","name":"Contour1","params":{"bottom_z":{"reference":"top_of_model","offset":-10}}}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"generate","arguments":{}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"verify","arguments":{}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"post","arguments":{"output":"contour.nc","post":"Fanuc"}}}
```

- `verify`: Contour1 has status ok and **0 warnings** (10 mm deep, inside the 15 mm flutes). The only finding is the gate's: `gouge: program cuts below the model in 1 cell(s), worst 10.00 mm at (22.32, 19.71, z 10.00)`.
- `post` is refused with the same line.

### What the toolpath actually does there

I checked it in a scratch app test: the same job built through the commands, every move's chords at 0.5 µm against the gouge column.

- The column's centre is (22.31802, 19.71006). The part's wall there is at y 19.71901 (the model's max Y), so the centre sits 9 µm inside the part.
- The nearest the tool centre ever comes to that point is **3.00895 mm** (move 368, a feed at z 15). With r = 3, the cutter edge stays **9 µm outside** the column centre. The path is exactly on the wall, as it should be.
- The sim (`stock_sim::simulate_document`, field arm, 0.375 mm cells) still reads that column's top at z 10, the contour's floor, so `deviate_field` reports `sim - part = 10 - 20 = -10`: a 10 mm gouge.

### Why

- `march_verdicts::deviate_field` (and the column engine's `deviate`) judge each column by height alone: the marched top at the column centre minus the part's top there. At a vertical wall, a column whose centre is a few µm inside the part flips from "full height" to "floor" on a sideways error far below the field's resolution. That error then reads as a gouge the depth of the wall.
- The viewer's eye doesn't do this. `preview::gate_tol(tol, cell)` judges a hit point by its distance to the model, with the march's landing slack (`HIT_GATE = 0.15` cells) added, and PR #288 reuses that for the machined mesh. So the post gate and the viewer can disagree about the same program.
- Whether a column centre lands in that sliver depends on the stock lattice's phase against the wall. I think that's why `lead_approach.rs`, which posts a contour on this same part in a box stock at z -7, doesn't hit it. I haven't checked that.
- A 3D Finish (BN-0600, kind defaults) on the same part with the same stock is refused with 37 gouge columns, the worst also at (22.32, 19.71) and the rest along the D's curved wall. That looks like the same mechanism, but I haven't measured those columns.

### Possible fixes (owner's call - the gouge law is the Prime Directive's)

1. Judge a gouge column against the **lowest part top within a lateral slack** of its centre (for example `gate_tol(DEV_TOL, cell)`), so a column within the field's resolution of a wall isn't charged the wall's height. It still convicts any cut that reaches past the slack.
2. Or judge the program gate the way the preview does: the distance from the marched surface point to the model, with the same gate. The gate and the viewer would then share one law.

Either way, a pinning test is this job (or a synthetic plate whose wall sits a few µm off a lattice centre), plus the existing gouge goldens to show real gouges still block.

**Also in a realistic setup** (main 8cf3c90, scratch app test): the same plate in `lead_approach.rs`'s own box stock (70 x 70 x 27 at z -7).
- A 3D Finish (`BN-0600`, kind defaults) is refused: `gouge: program cuts below the model in 37 cell(s), worst 22.01 mm at (-26.56, 13.94, z -2.01)`. Generator verify reports no gouge (only `ShankHit`).
- At that column I sampled every move at 0.01 mm. The ball reaches the column's centre line down to z -2.0103, the sim's own reading, with the line **0.00002 mm inside the ball**. The finishing ball is tangent to the wall, as it should be, and the column verdict charges the tangency as a 22 mm gouge.
- Boundary: in the same stock, a contour 10 mm deep is clean, which fits the verdict depending on where the lattice falls against the wall.

That narrows the cause. For the finish, the field reads the ball exactly, so the fault is the column verdict itself (`deviate_field` / `deviate`), not field interpolation. The contour case above (a cutter edge 9 um outside the centre, read as cut) still needs field slack on top of that.
**Root cause (confirmed):** `stock_sim::march_verdicts::deviate_field` charges a column by height alone, so a column centre 9 um inside the wall that the sim reads as cut becomes a 10 mm gouge. Measured: the cutter edge stays 9 um outside that centre, and the column reads z 10.

**Root cause (likely), not instrumented:** why the field reads that column as cut at all. My guess is the field's interpolation at 0.375 mm cells, but I didn't measure the march there.

Suggested labels (I can't set them): `bug`, `P1` (a clean program a user posts is refused), `area:sim`, `source:agent`.

title: Documentation site: a docs folder published with GitHub Pages (user guide + architecture)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

body:
## Summary

CamCraft has no user-facing documentation. Everything a user needs (install, first run, what each operation does, how to read a refusal) is either in the README or in the owner's head, and everything a developer needs (crate map, command/undo model, testing tiers, release process) lives in `AGENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and `docs/` design notes that were written for the agents building it, not for people using or extending it.

This issue proposes a documentation site: a `docs/` source tree built with **mdBook** and published with **GitHub Pages**, containing

1. a **user guide** (install, UI tour, setups/stock/WCS, tools, operations, simulation and verification, posts and machines, the MCP server, troubleshooting and refusals, FAQ);
2. an **architecture / developer guide** (crate map, ECS and commands/undo, layering rules, testing tiers and gate, release process, contributing, clean-room protocol);
3. a link to the **API reference** (`cargo doc` output built in the same pipeline and placed under `/api/`).

Research is not finished: the open questions below (versioning, custom domain, repo visibility, and what counts as "in sync" with releases) need decisions before this can be broken into implementation issues. Nothing here is to be built until those are answered.

## Goals

- A new user can install, open a model and post a verified program from the guide alone.
- A new developer can find the crate that owns a behaviour, the command that changes it, and the gate that proves it, in under five minutes.
- Refusals are explained: each refusal the app can emit by name has an entry saying what it means and what to change.
- The site builds cheaply, deploys only on purpose, and cannot silently drift from the code (link check, PR checklist).
- Internal notes in `docs/` keep working for agents and for `docs/decisions/` and are not published.

Non-goals: translating the site; replacing `AGENTS.md` (which stays the agent contract); publishing `ROADMAP.md`, `RECOMMENDED.md` or the decision ledger; hosting the binaries (they stay on GitHub Releases).

## Current state (verified in the repo)

- `docs/` holds four internal notes only: `CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`, `M4.1-CRATE-SPLIT.md`, `M5-PHASE5-PLAN.md`, `spike-egui-go-no-go.md`. There is no `docs/decisions/` folder on `main` yet, although `AGENTS.md` and the agent workflow refer to one (issue branches write `docs/decisions/<N>-<slug>.md`).
- `README.md` has the product description, a download section, build instructions, testing, workspace layout, project documents and issue reporting. It is the only user-facing text.
- Crates (`crates/`): `app`, `cl`, `geometry`, `kernel`, `motion`, `post`, `sim`, `tools`, `ui`. Each crate's one-line purpose needs confirming from its `lib.rs` header when the architecture guide is written; `AGENTS.md` names `geometry`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion` as the M4.1 split.
- `assets/`: `ui/` (Tabler-derived toolbar/tree PNGs, `LICENSES.md`, `fonts/`), `posts/` (`.cps` post scripts, plus an `AGENTS.md` inside), `machines/` (`.mch` machine files, plus an `AGENTS.md`), `themes/`, `scripts/`.
- `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/` holds egui snapshot goldens, so the UI can already be rendered headlessly for screenshots.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (one row per behaviour change, `commit | date | change | version`) and `RELEASE_NOTES.md` exist; release notes per cut are written by the release process.
- `scripts/` has `gate.ps1` (gate tiers), `release.ps1`, `sign.ps1`, `installer.ps1`, and packaging scripts for Linux (AppImage, Flatpak, Snap), macOS, and a `README.md`.
- Workflows: `ci.yml` (manual `workflow_dispatch`), `nightly.yml` (manual/nightly), `release.yml` (tags `vX.Y.0` plus `workflow_dispatch`), `aur-package.yml`. No Pages workflow exists.
- Actions budget (`AGENTS.md`): 3000 minutes per month, Windows 2x, macOS 10x, and no `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` triggers without the owner's say-so.
- Repo is `NeoTech/Camcraft`. Whether it is public (Pages on a private repo needs a paid plan) is not verified here; see open questions.

## Options compared

| Option | Pros | Cons | Actions cost | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **mdBook** | Rust-native and the rust-lang standard (`rust-lang/book`, `rustc-dev-guide` use it). Built-in search. Single binary, Markdown plus `SUMMARY.md`, fast builds. Preprocessors for mermaid (`mdbook-mermaid`) and link checking (`mdbook-linkcheck`, and the `mdbook-linkcheck2` fork that rustc-dev-guide uses). | No versioning; no first-class multi-version site. Mermaid and link check are third-party preprocessors to pin. Less theming than Docusaurus. | ~1-3 billed minutes per run on `ubuntu-latest` (1x), dominated by installing the prebuilt binary; a `cargo install` would add many minutes, so do not compile it in CI. | **Best** for a book-shaped guide written by and for Rust developers. |
| **Zola** | Single binary, fast, Rust-based. | Search needs wiring (index generation plus a front-end). Mermaid via shortcode or JS. No versioning. Smaller ecosystem for docs. | Similar to mdBook (~1-3 min). | Workable, but more glue than mdBook for the same result. |
| **MkDocs Material** | Polished default theme; strong built-in search; `pymdownx.superfences` gives mermaid; `mike` provides per-version docs. | Python toolchain in CI (pip install, slower and more cache work); a second language ecosystem beside Rust. | ~2-4 min (pip install dominates unless cached). | Strong alternative if versioned docs are a must; costs a Python toolchain. |
| **Docusaurus** | Versioned docs are first-class (`docs:version`); MDX; good theming. | Node/npm toolchain and heavier builds (typically several minutes per run); search needs a plugin or Algolia; overkill for a single-product guide. | ~4-8 min per run (npm install and build). | Best versioning, but the heaviest to run and maintain. |

Notes on the table: Perplexity's sources directly substantiate mdBook's built-in search, its use by rust-lang, and `rustc-dev-guide`'s use of mdbook-linkcheck2 and mdbook-mermaid. Feature details for Zola, MkDocs Material and Docusaurus are from general knowledge and must be checked against their official docs before any of them is chosen. Current versions observed: `mdbook-linkcheck` v0.7.7, `mdbook-mermaid` v0.17.1 (both from release listings, not verified for compatibility with the mdBook version we would pin).

Publishing source, both are viable with the same generator:

- **Actions artifact + `actions/upload-pages-artifact` + `actions/deploy-pages`**: the site is built in CI and never committed. Recommended. Pages is then configured to "GitHub Actions" as source.
- **Branch + folder (`/docs` on a `gh-pages` branch)**: requires committing generated HTML, which conflicts with "generated output is never committed" (the graphify rule applies the same way). Rejected.

## Recommendation

**mdBook**, published by an Actions workflow that uploads the built book as a Pages artifact.

Reasons:

1. It is the Rust-standard tool for this shape of document; contributors who know Rust know its layout.
2. Built-in search with no extra setup, which is the thing users ask for first.
3. Its CI is one binary download plus a build, which is the cheapest of the four on the Actions budget.
4. The source is plain Markdown in the repo, reviewable in the same PR flow as code (see the PR checklist below).
5. Versioning is the one real gap. For a pre-1.0 app that cuts minor releases, "latest plus the last release tag" is enough at first; a versioned tree is a follow-up decision (open questions).

Revisit only if the versioned-docs requirement becomes hard before 1.0; then MkDocs Material + `mike` is the fallback.

## Proposed folder layout

Keep the existing internal notes and the book source apart so mdBook only reads what is meant to be published:

```
docs/
  CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md            internal design notes (unchanged, not published)
  M4.1-CRATE-SPLIT.md            internal
  M5-PHASE5-PLAN.md              internal
  spike-egui-go-no-go.md         internal
  decisions/                     internal decision records (not published)
  guide/                         NEW - the published site (mdBook project root)
    book.toml                    mdBook config (src = "src", mermaid + linkcheck preprocessors)
    src/
      SUMMARY.md                 the table of contents; the only index of the book
      intro.md
      user/                      user guide
        install.md
        first-run.md
        ui-tour.md               panes, ribbon, browser, properties
        setups-stock-wcs.md
        tools-library.md
        operations/              one page per operation family
          2d.md  3d.md  drilling.md  turning.md  multiaxis.md  probe.md
        heights-linking.md
        simulation.md            rest material, gouge, deviation
        posts-machines.md        .mch and .cps
        mcp-server.md            MCP server for AI agents
        troubleshooting.md       refusals, read by name
        faq.md
      dev/                       architecture / developer guide
        architecture.md          crate map and layering rules
        ecs-commands-undo.md
        testing-gates.md         tiers (quick/batch/release), where tests live
        release.md               the cut process as a reader sees it
        contributing.md          claim-by-comment, draft PRs, clean-room
        clean-room.md
      api.md                     pointer to the cargo doc output at /api/
    images/                      our own renders only (see Assets policy)
  guide/book/                    BUILD OUTPUT - gitignored, never committed
```

- Internal notes stay in `docs/` root and `docs/decisions/` and are not referenced from the book. The book does not link to internal notes; where a user-facing fact lives only in a note, the fact is moved into the book.
- `docs/guide/book/` is ignored by git (`.gitignore`), and the Pages artifact is built from it, not committed.
- `README.md` stays the product front page; it links to the site once it exists. The site does not replace it.
- API reference: `cargo doc --no-deps` for the workspace crates, copied to `site/api/` by the workflow. Crates not marked `publish = false` need confirming; this is about links to rustdoc, not crates.io.

File naming: lowercase, hyphenated, one topic per file; `SUMMARY.md` is the only index. Each operation family page is named by the family (`2d.md`), not by vendor or HSMWorks name.

Ownership: the owner (NeoTech) approves structure and voice; each feature PR that changes user-visible behaviour updates the matching page (see Maintenance). Agents draft pages in their issue branch like any other change.

## Publishing pipeline

- **Trigger:** `workflow_dispatch` (manual) and tag push on minor/major tags only, matching `release.yml`'s `vX.Y.0` rule, so a docs build happens at each cut and on demand. No `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger (AGENTS.md Actions budget). Patch tags build nothing (release law).
- **Cost:** one `ubuntu-latest` job (1x multiplier), ~1-3 billed minutes, roughly one run per minor cut plus manual runs. Against 3000 minutes/month this is negligible; the cost is in the manual runs, so keep the job to: checkout, install prebuilt mdBook and two preprocessors (pinned versions, no `cargo install`), `mdbook build`, `cargo doc --no-deps`, link check, upload, deploy.
- **Deploy method:** `actions/configure-pages`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, `actions/deploy-pages`, with the `github-pages` environment. Two jobs: `build` (contents: read) and `deploy` (pages: write, id-token: write). Permissions set per job, not at top level, as in `release.yml`.
- **Branch/permissions:** Pages source set to "GitHub Actions" in repo settings (a one-time owner step); no `gh-pages` branch; no write to `main`.
- **Custom domain (optional):** configured in Settings → Pages with DNS records. With a custom Actions workflow, GitHub does not create the CNAME for you; the domain setting itself is what counts. Decide whether to add a `CNAME` file to the artifact (Perplexity's sources say it is not needed for an Actions-published site; verify before relying on it).
- **Versioning per release tag:** not decided. See open questions. Default proposal: the site always shows the latest release's docs; each cut's book is archived under `/vX.Y/` only once the versioning decision is made.
- **Link check:** `mdbook-linkcheck` on the built book (internal links and, optionally, external links with a retry budget) so a broken anchor fails the run. External link checking is noisy; default to internal links only and treat external as a warning.
- **Failure policy:** a failed docs build must not block a release tag's binary build (separate workflow, no `needs:` between them).

## Content outline

### User guide

1. **Install** - Windows installer and zip, Linux packages (TAR.GZ, DEB, RPM, AppImage, Snap, Flatpak), macOS (ZIP, DMG), AUR source package; where binaries come from (GitHub Releases); unsigned-build note (signing is secret-gated, see `release.yml`); first-launch warning text on each OS described in our own words.
2. **First run and UI tour** - opening a model (STL, OBJ, STEP); panes and the ribbon; the operation browser and the properties panel; keyboard and mouse picking; undo and redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) and what they cover.
3. **Setups, stock and WCS** - creating a setup; stock shape and size; work offsets G54-G59; fixtures; machine choice (mill, 5-axis, lathe, mill-turn).
4. **Tools and tool library** - tool types, creating and editing a tool, the tool catalogue, holder and flute checks that the app enforces.
5. **Operations by family** - one page each:
   - 2D: face, contour (G41/G42 compensation), pocket, adaptive clearing, slot, trace, engrave, chamfer, circular, bore, thread milling;
   - 3D: adaptive roughing per level, waterline, parallel, scallop, radial, spiral, morph, flow, pencil, steep/shallow finishing;
   - drilling: spot, drill, peck, deep, tap, bore cycles and hole recognition;
   - turning: lathe operations and the spindle law;
   - multi-axis: 3+2 indexing, rotary contour/parallel/offset, 5-axis operations;
   - probe: whatever probe operations exist when the page is written (confirm, do not invent).
   Each page: what it is for, its parameters (named as the UI shows them), when to use it, what it refuses, a worked example with our own screenshot.
6. **Heights and linking** - clearance, retract, top, bottom heights; lead-in and lead-out; links between passes.
7. **Simulation and verification** - rest material; gouge and collision checks; deviation; what "verified" means and what it does not guarantee; the rule that unsafe output is blocked, not warned.
8. **Posts and machines** - choosing a post processor; `.cps` post scripts; `.mch` machine files; the intermediate (CLFile/`.cnc`) that posts read; dry-run advice.
9. **MCP server for AI agents** - what it exposes, how to connect an agent, what it can and cannot change (it goes through the same command history as the UI).
10. **Troubleshooting and refusals** - the refusal taxonomy: each refusal the app prints is listed by its name with the cause and the fix; how to read the diagnostic; what to send in a bug report.
11. **FAQ**.

### Architecture / developer guide

1. **Architecture overview** - the crate map from `crates/` with one-line purposes; the layering rule (ui -> app -> flecs; UI never calls `sys_*` or world-level APIs directly); where geometry, toolpaths, post and sim sit.
2. **ECS, commands and undo** - components declared in `crates/app/src/schema.rs`; the command history as single source of truth for undo/redo; ephemeral UI state is not undoable; deleting an entity frees its cached toolpath and mesh.
3. **Testing and gates** - the three tiers (quick, batch, release) from `scripts/gate.ps1`; where test binaries live; golden CLFile/G-code files under `tests/golden/`; the `crates/ui` CWD rule for snapshots.
4. **Release process** - how a minor/major cut is made (PR review, merge, release branch, tag, `release.yml` artifacts); why patch versions are not cut.
5. **Contributing** - claim-by-comment on issues; draft PRs; the `source:agent` label; labels (`P0`-`P2`, `area:*`); the commit format (conventional commits, `Fixes #N`).
6. **Clean-room protocol** - what the project does and does not use as reference (published Autodesk user docs for behaviour only; public G-code standards; handbooks; our own notes), in our own words, with the one-line provenance comment rule for modules.

## Screenshots and assets policy

- Screenshots show **our UI only**, rendered by us. Preferred source: the egui snapshot harness in `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/`, so images can be regenerated when the UI changes (a script or test that writes to `docs/guide/src/images/`).
- No HSMWorks or Autodesk screenshots, icons, text or sample output of any kind. Model and part images are generated fixtures we own.
- Icons referenced in the book come from `assets/ui/` and stay under the license recorded in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`; the book credits nothing new.
- Images are PNG, sized for the book (no multi-megabyte screenshots); a stale-image check belongs in the follow-up issue.
- Operation-specific glyphs are drawn by us, as `AGENTS.md` requires.

## Maintenance

- **Who updates docs:** the author of a behaviour-changing PR updates the matching page in the same PR. A new operation or refusal adds its page or entry in the same PR that adds it.
- **PR checklist:** a `docs:` checklist item in the PR template (or the existing PR body) asking "does this change a user-visible behaviour, a refusal name or a crate's role? If yes, the matching `docs/guide/` page is updated." This is an AGENTS.md change and needs the owner's approval before it lands (process law).
- **Link check:** runs in the docs workflow on each cut and on demand; internal links are gating.
- **Sync with releases:** each cut's `CHANGELOG.md` row for a user-visible change has a docs entry or a `Docs:` line in the PR; the cut checklist confirms the site was built from the tag.
- **Stale-doc detection:** not automated in the first version; checked at each cut by the release process (a checklist item, not a CI job, to keep the Actions budget).

## Open questions (need decisions before breakdown)

1. **Repo visibility and Pages availability:** is `NeoTech/Camcraft` public? If private, does the owner's plan include Pages on private repos? (Affects whether this is buildable at all.)
2. **Versioning:** latest-only, or a versioned tree (`/vX.Y/`)? If versioned, how: archive copies on a `gh-pages` branch (which conflicts with the "no generated output committed" rule unless the branch is deploy-only), or build every tag in the same workflow (more minutes per run, reproducible)? Recommend deciding after the first minor cut ships.
3. **Custom domain:** wanted or not? If yes, which domain, and does the CNAME live in the artifact or only in the Pages settings?
4. **Generator confirmation:** accept mdBook? Confirm the preprocessors (`mdbook-mermaid`, `mdbook-linkcheck` vs `mdbook-linkcheck2`) and their pinned versions against the pinned mdBook version. Verify the Zola, MkDocs and Docusaurus claims in the table against their official docs before a final choice.
5. **Folder name:** `docs/guide/` (proposed) vs `book/` at the repo root vs `site/`. Decide once; the choice is in every link.
6. **Screenshot pipeline:** does the owner want the snapshot harness to write book images (a new test-side writer, so it is a `crates/ui` change), or are images hand-captured per release?
7. **Docs license:** text under the repo license, or a separate license (e.g. CC-BY) for the guide? The image and icon licenses in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` must be respected either way.
8. **PR checklist wording:** the docs item in the PR template changes process; owner approves the wording (AGENTS.md change).
9. **Refusal catalogue source:** should the refusal list be generated from the code (a list of refusal names with a test that every name is documented) or written by hand? Generated is safer against drift and is recommended, but it needs a decision on where the list lives.
10. **Audience and tone:** one guide for both users and developers, or two sites? Proposed: one book, two parts (`user/`, `dev/`), each with its own table-of-contents heading.

## Proposed breakdown into follow-up issues

Each becomes its own issue after the open questions are answered:

- [ ] Decide open questions 1-10 and record each decision in `RECOMMENDED.md` (or `docs/decisions/`).
- [ ] Scaffold `docs/guide/` (`book.toml`, `SUMMARY.md`, empty pages) and `.gitignore` for the build output; builds locally with `mdbook build`.
- [ ] Add the docs workflow (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`, `workflow_dispatch` + minor/major tags, pinned installs, Pages artifact + deploy, link check) and the one-time owner step (Pages source = GitHub Actions).
- [ ] Write the user guide: install and first run, UI tour.
- [ ] Write the user guide: setups, stock, WCS, tools library.
- [ ] Write the user guide: operations by family (one issue per family, five families).
- [ ] Write the user guide: heights and linking, simulation and verification, posts and machines.
- [ ] Write the user guide: MCP server, troubleshooting and refusals, FAQ.
- [ ] Write the developer guide: architecture overview (crate map from each crate's header), ECS/commands/undo.
- [ ] Write the developer guide: testing and gates, release process, contributing, clean-room.
- [ ] Add `cargo doc` output to the site under `/api/`.
- [ ] Snapshot-based image pipeline for `docs/guide/src/images/` (if decided in question 6).
- [ ] PR template docs checklist item and cut checklist entry (owner approval of wording first).
- [ ] Versioned docs (only if question 2 chooses it).
- [ ] Custom domain (only if question 3 chooses it).
- [ ] Update `README.md` to link the published site.

## Done means

- `mdbook build` succeeds locally and in the docs workflow with pinned tools, with no warnings from the link check.
- The published site at the Pages URL shows: install, first run, every operation family, troubleshooting/refusals, the crate map, the testing tiers and the release process, each reachable from the table of contents.
- The docs workflow runs only on `workflow_dispatch` and minor/major tags (checked in the YAML), costs no more than the estimate on the run's Actions summary, and its trigger list is what this issue says.
- No internal design note, decision record or roadmap file is published; the artifact contains only the built `docs/guide/` tree and the `api/` output.
- Every screenshot in the book is an image of our UI, with its generator named on the page or in the build notes.
- The PR checklist and cut checklist include the docs step, approved by the owner.
- `README.md` links to the site.

## References

- mdBook guide: https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/
- mdBook CI guide (building and deploying): https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/continuous-integration.html
- mdBook repository: https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook
- rust-lang book (built with mdBook): https://github.com/rust-lang/book
- rustc developer guide (mdBook, mdbook-linkcheck2, mdbook-mermaid): https://github.com/rust-lang/rustc-dev-guide
- GitHub Pages custom workflows: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages
- actions/deploy-pages: https://github.com/actions/deploy-pages
- GitHub Pages custom domains: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/managing-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site
- mdbook-mermaid: https://github.com/badboy/mdbook-mermaid
- mdbook-linkcheck: https://github.com/Michael-F-Bryan/mdbook-linkcheck
- MkDocs Material (fallback): https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/
- Docusaurus versioning (rejected for now): https://docusaurus.io/docs/versioning
- Repo rules that constrain this: `AGENTS.md` (Clean-Room Protocol; Testing; Commits and Releases; Actions budget); `scripts/README.md` (gate tiers); `.github/workflows/release.yml` (tag trigger and permissions pattern).

title: Take pixel snapshot goldens out of the PR flow; structural UI tests instead

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
## Problem

The UI suites compare rendered frames pixel-for-pixel against PNG goldens committed under `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/` (`egui_app.png`, `egui_app_light.png`, `egui_tool_editor.png`, ...). In the PR flow this costs more than it catches:

- **Every UI PR rewrites the same shared binaries.** PNGs can't merge, so any two open UI PRs conflict, and each merge re-conflicts the rest. On 2026-11-08, #201, #213, #232 and #234 each needed a maintainer refresh, and #213 and #232 needed it twice.
- **A regenerated golden proves little.** The fix for each conflict was to re-run with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`, which accepts whatever the merged tree renders, so a real layout regression is accepted with it.
- **They're platform-sensitive.** A macOS run showed 1–4 px diffs on unchanged UI (the #234 review); the #201 review saw 5,328 scattered pixels. Real changes get lost in that noise.

## Proposal

1. **Take pixel snapshots out of the PR flow.** Mark the snapshot tests `#[ignore]` as a heavy-lane test named in the ignore reason, run at minor/major cuts via `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier release`, and regenerated once at the cut in one commit. PRs never touch `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/*.png`.
2. **Replace them in the PR suite with structural UI tests.** egui_kittest exposes the AccessKit tree: assert that widgets exist, their labels and state, panel visibility, enabled/disabled cells, status-strip text. These are text-only assertions that diff and merge like code, are platform-independent, and fail with a readable message.
3. **Optional:** keep one pixel smoke test (the window renders non-blank) with a loose tolerance, in the same release lane.
4. **Process docs:** update AGENTS.md (Testing; drop the "regenerate goldens on merge" habit) and the gate maps, and say in the PR-review guidance that a PR must not change snapshot PNGs.

## Done means

- No test in the default/quick/batch tiers reads or writes `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/*.png`; the release tier runs them.
- Each existing pixel snapshot's intent is covered by at least one structural assertion.
- `#[test]` counts before and after match (moved to the ignored lane, not deleted).
- AGENTS.md and the review guidance are updated.

Sequencing: land after the open UI PRs that currently touch snapshots (#213, #232) merge, so this doesn't add another conflict on top.
